gold: Pyomyositis of the levator scapulae muscle caused by Fusobacterium necrophorum

selector.rationale: The presence of an intramuscular abscess in the left levator scapulae muscle as shown by MRI and a poorly defined collection in the left paraspinal musculature on CT scan strongly supports the diagnosis of Paraspinal abscess.

rejected.label: Pyogenic infection
rejected.why: Too broad, as it encompasses many types of infections, including the more specific diagnosis of Paraspinal abscess.

rejected.label: Cervical lymphadenitis
rejected.why: Lack of specific evidence pointing to lymph node involvement as the primary issue.

rejected.label: Fusobacterium necrophorum infection
rejected.why: While the microbiological culture shows F. necrophorum infection, this finding alone does not fully explain the clinical and imaging findings that point more directly to a Paraspinal abscess.

rejected.label: Lemierre's syndrome
rejected.why: Although it is a strong candidate due to the presence of F. necrophorum and signs of infection, the specific imaging findings of an intramuscular abscess in the paraspinal region make Paraspinal abscess a more precise diagnosis for the given clinical scenario.
